items.q: Find the mass of 5 moles of a substance of molar mass 18 g per mol.
items.s: Mass = moles × molar mass = 5 × 18 = 90 g.

items.q: 2.5 moles of a solute are dissolved to make 4 litres of solution. Find the molarity.

items.q: 200 ml of a 0.5 molar solution is diluted to give a 0.1 molar solution. Find the final volume in millilitres.
The theoretical yield of a reaction is 120 g and the actual yield obtained is 60 g. Find the percentage yield.
items.s: Percentage yield = (actual ÷ theoretical) × 100 = (60 ÷ 120) × 100 = 50 per cent.

items.q: 250 g of a reactant of molar mass 40 reacts completely according to a stoichiometry of 2 mol reactant to 3 mol product. The product has molar mass 64. Find the mass of product formed.
100 kg of a reactant is fed to a reactor and 60 kg reacts. Find the percentage conversion.
items.s: Conversion = (reacted ÷ fed) × 100 = (60 ÷ 100) × 100 = 60 per cent.

items.q: A reactor requires 100 kg of a reactant and is supplied 125 kg. Find the percentage excess.
items.s: Excess = 125 − 100 = 25 kg. Percentage excess = (25 ÷ 100) × 100 = 25 per cent.

items.q: A reaction gives 90 kg of the wanted product and 10 kg of an unwanted product. Find the selectivity to the wanted product as a percentage of total product.
items.s: Total product = 90 + 10 = 100 kg. Selectivity = (90 ÷ 100) × 100 = 90 per cent.

items.q: A reactor of working volume 2 cubic metres is fed at 4 cubic metres per minute. Find the residence time in minutes.

items.q: A feed of 20 cubic metres per hour passes through a catalyst bed of 5 cubic metres. Find the space velocity per hour.
items.s: Space velocity = flow ÷ volume = 20 ÷ 5 = 4 per hour.

items.q: A reactant enters a continuous stirred tank reactor at 20 mol per minute and 0.5 of it must react. The rate of reaction is 2 mol per minute per cubic metre. Find the reactor volume.
items.s: V = (feed × conversion) ÷ rate = (20 × 0.5) ÷ 2 = 5 cubic metres.

items.q: A stream of concentration 4 mol per litre flows at 2 litres per minute. Find the molar flow rate in mol per minute.
items.s: Molar flow = concentration × volumetric flow = 4 × 2 = 8 mol per minute.

items.q: 400 kg of a reactant is fed to a reactor and 150 kg reacts. Find the percentage conversion.
items.s: Conversion = (reacted ÷ fed) × 100 = (150 ÷ 400) × 100 = 37.5 per cent.

items.q: A reactor of working volume 20 cubic metres is fed at 4 cubic metres per minute. Find the residence time in minutes.
items.s: Residence time = volume ÷ flow = 20 ÷ 4 = 5 minutes.

items.q: A substance of molar mass 100 g per mol has a mass of 36 g. Find the number of moles.
items.s: Moles = mass ÷ molar mass = 36 ÷ 100 = 0.36 mol.

items.q: Find the mass of 10 moles of a substance of molar mass 40 g per mol.
items.s: Mass = moles × molar mass = 10 × 40 = 400 g.

items.s: Total product = 30 + 10 = 40 kg. Selectivity = (30 ÷ 40) × 100 = 75 per cent.

items.q: A reactant enters a continuous stirred tank reactor at 10 mol per minute and 0.5 of it must react. The rate of reaction is 2 mol per minute per cubic metre. Find the reactor volume.
items.s: V = (feed × conversion) ÷ rate = (10 × 0.5) ÷ 2 = 2.5 cubic metres.

items.q: 2 mol of gas is held at 5 atm and 400 K. Find its volume in cubic metres, taking R as 8.314 J per mol K and one atmosphere as 100 kilopascals.
A stream of 2 kg per second with a specific heat capacity of 4.18 kJ per kg K is heated through 50 K. Find the heat duty in kW.
items.s: Q = mass flow × specific heat × rise = 2 × 4.18 × 50 = 418 kW.

items.q: A separation unit receives 250 kg of a component in its feed and delivers 80 kg of it in the product. Find the percentage recovery.
items.s: Recovery = (product ÷ feed) × 100 = (80 ÷ 250) × 100 = 32 per cent.
